title: Ineos Grenadier Quartermaster
verdict: A Grenadier with a foot of extra frame and a bed that takes a Euro pallet, as long as you lift the spare out first. It's a seriously capable off-roader that happens to have a tailgate, and in America it carries a 25% chicken tax on top.

paragraphs: Most pickups start as trucks and get dressed up as lifestyle accessories. The Quartermaster went the other way. Ineos took the [[grenadier/station-wagon|Grenadier Station Wagon]], stretched its ladder frame by 305 mm, cut the roof off behind the second row and fitted a bed sized for a 1,200 × 800 mm Euro pallet. It still has coil springs at all four corners, Carraro beam axles and a BMW straight-six, so it rides and crawls like an expedition wagon with an open load bay. AutoDaily put it neatly: it's "more of a 4×4 with an open load area than what we would call a pick-up."

story.heading: FROM GOODWOOD TO HAMBACH
paragraphs: The Quartermaster made its public debut at the Goodwood Festival of Speed in July 2023, as wagon deliveries were only just starting in markets like Australia. Series production began in late 2023 on the same Hambach, France, line that builds the wagon, in the former Smart factory Ineos bought from Mercedes. European deliveries were due from December 2023, with Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Sub-Saharan Africa next. A cheaper cab-chassis for tray bodies was scheduled for later in 2024.

Australia mattered more than anywhere. Ineos said it expected 80% of its Australian Grenadier sales to be Quartermasters or cab-chassis models. That put it head to head with the [[land-cruiser/70-series|70 Series LandCruiser]] ute, which still has a leaf-sprung rear. Caravan World drove both and found the Ineos more compliant over small bumps and "blasts the 79 Series out of the water" off-road. The Toyota keeps the edge on payload, price and parts availability.

story.heading: WHAT THE EXTRA FOOT BUYS (AND COSTS)
paragraphs: The bed is 1,564 mm long and 1,619 mm wide, with 1,337 mm between the wheel arches, four lashing eyes and a 400 W power outlet. The tailgate takes 225 kg (about 496 lb) when it's down. Payload depends on market and engine: Ineos quotes up to 907 kg for an Australian petrol truck and 832 kg for the diesel, and about 1,675 lb at US launch. Towing stays at 3,500 kg (about 7,700 lb), the same as the wagon. Petrol output is unchanged at 282 hp; the diesel makes 550 Nm.

The extra length costs some geometry. Approach angle is a strong 36.2°, but breakover falls from the wagon's 28.2° to 26.2° and departure from 36.1° to 22.6°. That's why the spare wheel lives upright in the bed rather than under it, where it would hang down and cut the departure angle further. The catch is that you have to lift the spare out before a pallet will go in. Turning circle grows to about 14.5 m, roughly a metre more than the wagon, and Top Gear called that figure "genuinely appalling."

story.heading: THE AMERICAN PROBLEM
paragraphs: Ineos opened US orders in April 2024 at $86,900 for the base Quartermaster and $94,900 for the Trialmaster and Fieldmaster, all before destination. That was $15,400 more than the Station Wagon, and most of the difference was the 25% chicken tax on imported light trucks. The September 2024 production stoppage, caused by a parts shortage after supplier Recaro Automotive went insolvent, pushed US deliveries back, and the first cargo ship of Quartermasters reached America in March 2025. A month later, new US tariffs took the total import duty on the truck to 50%.

Ineos said it would absorb most of the extra tariff, but the US starting price still rose 11%, from $85,500 to $94,500 including shipping, according to Automotive News. Ineos told the paper the Quartermaster could reach up to 20% of its US volume and pitched it against the Rivian R1T and F-150 Raptor rather than a Silverado. Expedition Portal's long-term test truck towed a 5,000 lb trailer and drew this verdict: "Expect it to drive like the HD truck it is and not a car, and it won't disappoint."

story.heading: THE 2026 FIX AND THE BUILD SCENE
paragraphs: For 2026 the Quartermaster got the same fix as the wagon: a variable-ratio steering box that's firmer and more precise near straight-ahead, steering stops that cut the turning circle by about 5%, better climate-control components and a faster way to silence the Intelligent Speed Assist chime. A Black Edition joined the range, and in the US the base trim was dropped. The off-road hardware didn't change.

The aftermarket has been quicker than the factory. Norweld builds trays and canopies, Dirtbox Overland sells a $11,499 canopy camper made for the bed, and Leitner Designs makes a full-length roof rack that bolts to the roll cage rather than the gutters. Owners on the INEOS Forum fit Dirtbox caps, adjustable shocks and spare-wheel relocations, and Expedition Portal has filmed a Quartermaster on Letech portal axles. It's the closest thing on sale to a new 130-inch [[land-rover/defender-90-110|Defender]] pickup, and owners are building it that way.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE KAIJU
callout.title: Ineos Builds the Ute Australians Would Build
paragraphs: In December 2024 Ineos Australia revealed the Kaiju, a one-off Quartermaster built with local aftermarket partners to show how far the platform can go. It started as a Trialmaster with three lockers, a raised air intake, an auxiliary battery and factory bull bar, sliders and checker plates.

Norweld fitted an aluminium tray with a 1,200 mm trundle drawer, a 40-litre water tank and a Compact Deluxe Lite canopy holding a 130-litre fridge. REDARC supplied a 2,000 W inverter and 150 Ah lithium battery, Brown Davis a 168-litre long-range fuel tank, and JMACX remote-reservoir shocks replaced the factory dampers. It ran 315/70R17 mud-terrains. Ordered through Ineos retailers, selected parts from official accessory partners come with extended Ineos warranty.

engineering_intro: Under the bed, the Quartermaster is a stretched Grenadier. The box-section ladder frame is 305 mm longer, and everything bolted to it carries over: Carraro beam axles on five-link coil suspension with progressive-rate Eibach springs, permanent 4WD through a Tremec two-speed transfer case, and BMW six-cylinder engines with a ZF eight-speed automatic. The rear body is the wagon's up to the back doors, then it becomes a steel bed with a pallet-width floor.

engineering.v: Box-section ladder frame, 305 mm longer than the wagon
engineering.note: 3,227 mm (127 in) wheelbase; overall length 5,400 mm.
Progressive-rate Eibach springs on Carraro beam axles; no leaf springs.

engineering.v: BMW B58 petrol / B57 diesel 3.0 I6
engineering.note: Petrol 282 hp / 450 Nm (US only engine); diesel 245 hp / 550 Nm.
Permanent 4WD, 2.5:1 low range, centre lock; front and rear lockers on Trialmaster.
Takes one Euro pallet; four lashing eyes, 400 W outlet, 225 kg tailgate.
Kept off the underside to protect a 22.6° departure angle.

generations_table.note: The only engine sold in the US; 0–100 km/h in 8.8 s.
Europe, Australia, NZ and other markets; the big seller in Australia.
Bare chassis for trays such as Norweld's; sold in Australia and NZ, priced just below the tub truck.
Front and rear lockers, raised air intake, BFG KO2s; Expedition Portal's test truck added a factory winch.
Heated leather seats and comfort kit; aimed at lighter off-road use.
Variable-ratio steering, about 5% tighter turning circle, better HVAC; US base trim dropped.

buying_checks.head: Run the VIN at NHTSA
buying_checks.body: Recalls 23V828 (auxiliary switch relay wiring), 23V903 (steering ball-joint nuts) and 25V147 (door buttons) are filed against 2023–2024 Grenadiers. As of October 2026, NHTSA's recall database lists none for 2025–2026 models. Check every truck by VIN anyway, and get proof that any open campaign was closed.

buying_checks.head: Do the payload math before you buy a camper
buying_checks.body: Payload is modest for a pickup: about 1,675 lb at US launch, and 832–907 kg in Australia depending on engine. A canopy, fridge, water, a second battery and a winch use that up quickly. Expedition Portal's optioned Trialmaster was down to about 1,400 lb before any gear. In Australia, Caravan World quotes a GVM upgrade to roughly 3,900–4,000 kg for about A$5,800 plus fitting.

buying_checks.head: Know where the spare will live
buying_checks.body: From the factory the spare stands in the bed, sticks up above the bed sides and has to come out before a pallet will fit. It also gets in the way of flat tonneau covers. Ask whether the spare has been relocated (owners have moved it under the deck or under the rear axle) and check that the new mount is solid.

buying_checks.head: Drive it empty and on the highway
buying_checks.body: Several INEOS Forum owners describe an unladen Quartermaster as 'jittery' over bumps in a way the wagon isn't, though it settles once a canopy and gear go in. Pre-2026 trucks also have the slow, non-self-centring steering box and a 14.5 m turning circle. MY2026 trucks get the variable-ratio box and a turning circle about 5% tighter.

buying_checks.head: Wellside or cab-chassis?
buying_checks.body: Outside the US you can buy a cab-chassis and fit a tray. Ineos and Norweld offered early Australian cab-chassis buyers a A$7,000 tray contribution, with conditions. Caravan World lists Norweld trays from A$18,990 and canopies from A$19,205, so a tray build costs a lot more than the tub truck, but it gives you a flat, wider deck.

buying_checks.head: Confirm the lockers and Trialmaster kit
buying_checks.body: The centre diff lock is standard on every truck. Front and rear lockers come on the Trialmaster or with the Rough Pack. The locker switches are in the overhead panel, and the centre lock is on the transfer lever. Trialmaster trucks also get a raised air intake and all-terrain tires.

buying_checks.head: Check the bed for tie-down track and holes
buying_checks.body: Some dealers fit L-track to the bed and sides. One forum owner noted that some trucks were built without bed rails, so adding them means drilling and countersinking. Look for neat, sealed holes and no rust starting around the fasteners.

buying_checks.head: Ask about parts and the dealer
buying_checks.body: Caravan World scored parts access 7/10 against the LandCruiser. The engine and gearbox come from BMW and ZF, but body, bed and chassis parts come through Ineos's small network. Ask the nearest dealer about lead times, especially if you travel remote.

repairs.title: Engine oil and filter change (B58)
repairs.cost: About $150 for a dealer oil service, as quoted by a US Grenadier owner
repairs.symptoms: Service due, an 'Engine Oil Low' message, or the first break-in change. Towing and camper weight are good reasons to shorten intervals.
repairs.fix: This is the same job as on the wagon. Put the hood in its maintenance position and remove the engine cover. The canister filter housing is on top of the engine. Undo it with a 32 mm socket and replace the element and O-ring. Drain the sump, fit a new drain-plug washer, refill and check the level in the vehicle menu.
repairs.tools: 32 mm socket · drain pan · filter with O-ring and crush washer · oil: an owner quoted the manual as 6.5 L of 0W-20, ACEA C2 / BMW LL-17FE (check your own manual)

parts.name: BMW 0W-20 LL-17FE+ oil change kit for the B58 (7 L Genuine BMW oil + filter, O-ring, drain washer)

repairs.title: Engine air filter
repairs.symptoms: Service interval, or after dusty trail use. With a camper or tray, you'll be on gravel roads more than you think.
repairs.fix: Loosen the captive screws around the airbox (they don't come out) and lift off the top half. Note how the white felt pre-filter is fitted (glued to the filter on some trucks, clipped into the box on others), then swap the filter and close it up.
repairs.tools: PZ3 (Pozidriv #3) screwdriver · filter (a forum member reports Mahle LX3985/1 matches OEM; not officially confirmed)

parts.name: Mahle LX3985/1 air filter (owner-reported OEM match; not officially confirmed)
Mahle LX3985 BMW air filter (close sibling of LX3985/1; check it matches before buying)

repairs.title: Cabin air filter
repairs.time: ≈ 5–10 minutes once you know the trick
repairs.symptoms: Weak airflow or a musty smell, especially after dusty trips.
repairs.fix: This is the same as on the wagon. On a left-hand-drive truck, slide the passenger seat back, recline it and lie in the footwell with a headlamp. Unsnap the two clips under the filter frame, let the hinged plate swing down, pull the old filter out and fit the new one with the airflow arrow toward the cabin.
repairs.tools: Headlamp · curved pick · OEM INEOS #100326881, or Microguard 3692 reported to fit

parts.name: Microguard 3692 cabin air filter (owner-reported fit, no charcoal layer)
OEM INEOS cabin filter #100326881

repairs.title: Rear sag under a canopy or camper
repairs.cost: $599 for Owl/Eibach Pro-Lift springs (set of 4) or $765–795 for a Dirtbox air-bag kit, plus labor
repairs.symptoms: The rear sits low with a cap, fridge, water and batteries on board. The front bump stops get hit, and the truck tows nose-high.
repairs.fix: Weigh the truck loaded first. For a permanent build, Eibach's Pro-Lift springs (about +2.5 in. front, +1.2 in. rear; one kit for Grenadier and Quartermaster) restore height. Owl recommends matching bump stops. For a load that changes, Dirtbox sells a Traveler Mammoth rear air-bag kit that mounts at the factory bump-stop location with no drilling, in OEM-height and 2 in. versions. In Australia a GVM upgrade is the legal way to carry more.
repairs.tools: Floor jack · axle stands · torque wrench · kit instructions · bump stops to suit

parts.name: Grenadier lift springs Pro 2.5" (Eibach, also fits Quartermaster)
Eibach Pro-Lift springs for Grenadier
Grenadier & Quartermaster rear suspension air-bag kit

repairs.title: Unladen 'jitter': shock upgrade
repairs.symptoms: The ride feels busy and jittery over small bumps when the bed is empty. Forum owners say the wagon doesn't do this.
repairs.fix: Owners blame the longer wheelbase, the springs rated for payload, and possibly the bed mounts. One owner fitted Radflo adjustable shocks and reports a good ride on and off road. Another fitted MetalCloak suspension and still felt the jitter. Ineos's Kaiju build used JMACX remote-reservoir shocks. Adding the load you actually carry often settles it first, so try that before you spend money.
repairs.tools: Floor jack · axle stands · sockets · torque wrench · shocks specified for Quartermaster length

parts.name: Grenadier Shocks: Pro (and Quartermaster)
Grenadier TrailFlo suspension (and Quartermaster)

repairs.title: Relocate the spare out of the bed
repairs.symptoms: The spare blocks the pallet space, a flat tonneau or a canopy floor.
repairs.fix: Pick a mount that keeps the departure angle. Ineos put the spare in the bed because hanging it underneath costs ground clearance at the back. Forum owners have moved the spare under the deck (on a canopy build) or under the rear axle. Other options are a roof mount, which Ineos offers, or an aftermarket rear bumper with a carrier. Check the jack and lug wrench still reach.
repairs.tools: Sockets · torque wrench · relocation bracket or bumper from your chosen supplier

parts.name: INEOS roof-mounted spare wheel carrier and other factory accessories

repairs.title: Add L-track or O-track to the bed
repairs.symptoms: The four lashing eyes aren't enough for bikes, boxes or a drawer system.
repairs.fix: One owner's dealer fitted L-track on the bed floor and sides, which held a cargo bike sideways. The upper bed rails are held with plastic pop rivets on 8-inch centres. Another owner expects O-track to fit but says it may need shimming because the trim is recessed. On trucks without the rails fitted, drill, countersink and seal every hole.
repairs.tools: Drill · countersink · rivnut tool or bolts · sealant · track sections

parts.name: L-track bolt, M8, 4-pack
L-track tie-down ring with anchor mount, 4-pack

repairs.title: Diesel harshness at 1,700–2,000 rpm (non-US)
repairs.symptoms: Vibration or harshness at a steady 1,700–2,000 rpm on B57 diesel trucks.
repairs.fix: On a right-hand-drive diesel, one INEOS Forum owner found the 10 mm bolt holding the heat shield between the airbox and firewall loose. Tightening it removed about 90% of the harshness. Others traced rattles to an exhaust heat shield and to the heater pipes under the glovebox. These are owner fixes, not an Ineos bulletin.

parts.name: Heat-shield fastener (tighten the existing 10 mm bolt; replacements from an INEOS dealer)

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: The Quartermaster has the same axles and front suspension as the wagon, and it comes on LT265/70R17 or 255/70R18 (about 32 in.). Wagon owners on the INEOS Forum report 285/70R17 fits without rubbing and 285/75R17 (about 34 in.) fits on stock suspension. Treat 35s as the outer limit. One Quartermaster owner recommends narrow 35s on near-factory offset wheels, such as 255/85R17 or 35×10.5. Because the spare sits in the bed, there's no rear-door clearance problem like on the wagon, but a bigger spare stands taller in the bed. An owner at 7,000 ft stayed at 33s because of power loss on the factory gearing.

faq.q: How much payload does it have?
faq.a: It depends on market and engine. Ineos quoted 1,675 lb at US launch. In Australia it quotes 907 kg for the petrol and 832 kg for the diesel, against a 3,550 kg GVM. That's below most one-tonne utes and the 79 Series LandCruiser. Expedition Portal's optioned Trialmaster (winch, rack, dual batteries) had about 1,400 lb left.

3,500 kg braked (about 7,700 lb), the same as the wagon, with a 7,000 kg GCM and a 350 kg towball limit in Australian spec. With a heavy trailer and a loaded bed you'll reach the GCM and payload limits before the hitch rating.

faq.q: Will a Euro pallet really fit?
faq.a: Yes. There's 1,337 mm between the wheel arches, enough for a 1,200 × 800 mm pallet. You have to take the spare wheel out of the bed first.

It stands upright in the bed. Mounted underneath, it would cut into a departure angle that's already down to 22.6°. Ineos also offers a roof mount and a 15-litre lockable box that fits in the middle of the spare. Owners have moved it under the deck or under the rear axle.

faq.q: Can I get the diesel in the US?
faq.a: No. US trucks have only the BMW B58 3.0 petrol six (282 hp, 332 lb-ft). The B57 diesel (183 kW, 550 Nm) is sold in Europe, Australia, New Zealand and other markets.

faq.q: Why does it cost so much more than the wagon in the US?
faq.a: Mostly the 25% chicken tax on imported light trucks. At launch the Quartermaster cost $15,400 more than the Station Wagon. When new tariffs arrived in April 2025, total duty rose to 50%. Ineos said it would absorb most of that, but still raised the price 11%, to $94,500 including shipping.
faq.src: MOTOR AUTHORITY · YAHOO AUTOS · AUTOMOTIVE NEWS

faq.q: How does it drive compared with the wagon?
faq.a: It's much the same, with a longer turning circle: about 14.5 m against 13.5 m before 2026. Unladen it can feel jittery over small bumps, and it settles with weight in the bed. Expedition Portal found it quieter and more comfortable than the wagon. Top Gear noted the light rear end can lose grip on slippery climbs, which is where the lockers and all-terrain tires help.
faq.src: INEOS FORUM · EXPEDITION PORTAL · TOP GEAR

faq.q: What fuel economy does it get?
faq.a: Australian test-cycle figures are 12.6 L/100 km for the petrol and 10.5 L/100 km for the diesel. Edmunds lists 14 mpg combined for the US truck. Towing a caravan, Caravan World saw the high 20s in L/100 km from both engines. The tank holds 90 litres. Caravan World says about 10% of Australian Grenadier buyers fit a Brown Davis long-range tank, which adds 78 litres.

The engines haven't changed, so the main question is steering. MY2026 trucks have the variable-ratio box, about a 5% tighter turning circle, better HVAC and a quicker way to silence the speed-limit chime. Earlier trucks can be fitted with Owl's steering pump upgrade, which Owl says fits both the Grenadier and Quartermaster. Whichever year you buy, run the VIN for recalls.

faq.q: What camper and canopy options exist?
faq.a: Dirtbox Overland sells a canopy camper made for the Quartermaster bed for $11,499, and Norweld makes full-length, compact and half canopies plus trays. Leitner Designs makes a full-length roof rack (375 lb on-road, 200 lb off-road). INEOS Forum owners have fitted Dirtbox caps. Ineos's own accessory list includes a canvas tonneau, a roll-top cover and a hardtop.

mods.why: The bed is a pallet-width box with an upright spare in it. Canopies and canopy campers turn it into secure storage and a bed off the ground. Watch payload.
Restores ride height under a canopy and gear, and makes room for 34–35 in. tires. The springs and air bags fit both Grenadier bodies.

baseline_service.intro: Assume nothing was done early: the factory schedule is long (12 months / 12,000 miles in the US), the full service manual isn't sold to owners, and only dealers can reset the service counter. Baseline every fluid once, keep receipts with OEM-spec fluids to protect the 5-year warranty, and note that much of the drivetrain is shared with BMW (B58/B57 engines, ZF 8-speed), so FCP Euro and other BMW specialists carry many of the consumables. On a Quartermaster that has worked hard (towing, a camper or tray load), treat it as arduous use and shorten every interval.

items.spec: B58 petrol: 0W-20, ACEA C2 (dealers also cite C5 / API SP), BMW Longlife-17 FE+ · 6.5 L per the manual as quoted by owners; buy 7 L. B57 diesel: 0W-30 (the diesel manual lists Petronas Syntium 7000 E 0W-30) · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]

items.spec: Fuchs Titan Sintopoid 75W-90 (75W-85 also acceptable) · 1.8 L, or 2.64 L if the oil cooler and lines are drained too
items.interval: Dealer schedule: check every 2 years, replace at 6 years. Owners change it much earlier: one found metal flakes at 800 mi, and some trucks had it changed under recall at ~5,000 km.
items.note: O-ring-sealed drain and fill plugs, 15 Nm. Fill to spill isn't reliable because the cooler lines drain back, so measure what comes out.

parts.name: Fuchs Titan Sintopoid 75W-90, 1 L (buy 3)

items.spec: SAE 80W-90 GL-5 · 2.1 L per axle (workshop-manual figure quoted on the INEOS Forum). Note: Agile Offroad's diff-cover instructions call for 75W-140.
items.interval: First change at 12 months / 12,000 mi, then 60,000 mi per the US schedule as quoted by owners. Owners who wade or tow do it every 10,000 mi.
items.note: Remove the FILL plug first, because owners have snapped fill plugs after draining. 12 mm hex plugs (M22×1.5), 31 Nm; INEOS plug part GRA-5000-021220 (the O-ring isn't sold separately). The fill plug is magnetic. Same fluid with or without the lockers.

parts.name: Fuchs Titan Supergear MC 80W-90 gear oil, 1 L (buy 5)

items.note: If the date is unknown, flush it, especially after water crossings.

parts.name: Genuine BMW DOT 4 brake fluid (12 fl oz)

items.interval: Check level and condition at every service
items.note: The recirculating-ball steering is hydraulic. Owners with big tires and heavy steering look at Owl's upgraded pump. Check for leaks at the box and pump.

items.spec: Retorque suspension and body mounts; clear the body and safari-hatch drains
items.interval: At purchase, then every annual service
items.note: Dealer first-service packages include a suspension retorque and drain clearing. Run the VIN for open recalls (door button 25V147, steering ball-joint nut 23V903, aux switch panel 23V828) before anything else.

items.interval: Test at purchase and every service
items.note: Dealers include a battery health test in the annual service. Trucks that sat on a lot often have a tired battery, which causes odd electrical warnings.
